raw_response:
I would keep my farm anchored on the wheat-maize rotation and use the rest for cash crops that I can still manage well with four people in the household. On 225 mu, I would put 150 mu into wheat followed by summer maize, because that is the most familiar and stable part of my system and I have well irrigation to protect yield in dry spells. I would keep chili at 45 mu and stevia at 30 mu instead of expanding them too much, because they bring cash but they also need closer field management, more spraying, and more labor at key times. For wheat, I would use improved seed, keep fertilizer moderate but solid, irrigate at the key stages, and aim for steady grain output rather than chasing the highest possible yield. For maize, I would use hybrid seed and no-tillage after wheat harvest so I can save time and hold moisture. For chili and stevia, I would use better seed, give them more potassium and more irrigation than grain crops, and stay on top of pests because that is where income can be lost quickly. Overall, I would make conservative, workable decisions that fit my land, my labor, and the fact that I want both grain security and cash income.
